proposed_concepts.name: Asymmetric Relational Effort Trap
proposed_concepts.definition: The dysfunctional dynamic where one partner shoulders the vast majority of relationship initiation, planning, and emotional maintenance, leading to exhaustion, resentment, and loss of respect.

proposed_concepts.name: Autonomous Absence Scarcity Principle
proposed_concepts.definition: The psychological rule that persistent over-availability and desperate pursuit extinguish longing, whereas healthy physical and emotional absence creates the cognitive room for curiosity and desire.

proposed_concepts.name: Behavior-First Boundary Calibration
proposed_concepts.definition: The interpersonal intervention principle requiring behavioral self-containment, priority resets, and boundary enforcement to precede verbal negotiation, preventing premature emotional dumping.

proposed_concepts.name: The Walk-Away Relational Threshold
proposed_concepts.definition: The foundational emotional capacity to walk away from mistreatment or lack of reciprocity, overcoming abandonment panic to maintain self-worth and non-negotiable standards.

extracted_claims.statement: Constantly expressing desperate longing and double-texting prevents a partner from feeling your absence and destroys the cognitive space required to foster organic desire.

extracted_claims.statement: When relational effort is distributed asymmetrically (e.g., 90% from one partner and 10% from the other), the dynamic is structurally unhealthy and unsustainable.
A romantic relationship must remain a subordinate component of a balanced life rather than replacing one's career, health, family, and personal priorities.
Effective interpersonal re-calibration requires establishing behavioral independence and boundaries before engaging in verbal explanations or emotional discussions.

extracted_claims.statement: The ultimate prerequisite for self-respect and relational correction is the genuine, non-bluffing willingness to walk away from a partner who mistreats you.
Entering an intimate relationship requires psychological acceptance that the partner may leave and that one's life can fully endure and continue without them.

proposed_relationships.evidence_snippet: In your relationship, 90% of the effort is from your side and 10% from hers... you will just carry this burden on your shoulders and end up hurting yourself.
Saying 'I miss you' ten times a day won't make her start missing you... You aren't even letting her feel your absence.
We will show behavior first. Then we will move to the verbal... first behavior, then verbal. It is the most important part.
If you don't treat me well, I will walk away... Before entering a relationship, you must know that this person can also leave you. My life can go on without her too.
